_comment: Batch 10 (Sets 18-19). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason.

RN-S18-01.B: A client 1 day after cataract surgery who reports mild scratchiness in the operative eye and wants to know if it's normal
RN-S18-01.C: A client whose hearing aid is whistling and who would like an appointment to have it checked this week
RN-S18-01.D: A client with Ménière's disease requesting a refill of meclizine before the pharmacy closes this evening

RN-S18-04.A: "Follow a high-sodium diet to maintain your fluid balance and reduce the dizziness you feel between attacks."
RN-S18-04.C: "Increase your caffeine intake to improve alertness and help you feel steadier during the day."
RN-S18-04.D: "You can continue to drive as usual during an attack, as long as you pull over if it gets bad."

RN-S18-07.A: "Hold ice packs in your hands for a few minutes each day to toughen your fingers."
RN-S18-07.C: "Drink more caffeinated coffee or tea to keep your circulation going."
RN-S18-07.D: "Soak your fingers in cold water every day to help them adjust to the cold."

RN-S18-08.A: Completely on the left (nonoperative) side, supported with pillows behind the back
RN-S18-08.C: Prone, with a small pillow under the chest and abdomen for comfort
RN-S18-08.D: Trendelenburg position, with the head of the bed lower than the feet

RN-S18-09.A: "I'll use the CPAP only on nights when I feel especially tired or have been snoring."
RN-S18-09.C: "I'll take a sleeping pill every night at bedtime so that I can tolerate the mask until morning."
RN-S18-09.D: "After a few weeks of using the CPAP every night, my sleep apnea will be cured and I can stop."

RN-S18-10.B: "It cures influenza within 24 hours of taking the first dose."
RN-S18-10.C: "Taking it replaces the need for a yearly flu vaccine in the future."
RN-S18-10.D: "It works only if it is started after a full week of symptoms."

RN-S18-11.A: Serve very hot foods and drinks to relax the facial muscles before chewing
RN-S18-11.C: Encourage vigorous brushing of the teeth after each meal to prevent decay
RN-S18-11.D: Apply an ice pack to the face for several minutes before each meal

RN-S18-13.A: "There's no genetic risk for you, because Huntington's disease is caused by environmental exposures rather than by genes you inherit."
RN-S18-13.C: "Only sons can inherit Huntington's disease from an affected father, so daughters in the family are not at risk."
RN-S18-13.D: "The chance is 25%, which is the same risk as for inherited conditions in which both parents carry the gene."

RN-S18-14.A: "Take ibuprofen as needed for any headaches or muscle aches."
RN-S18-14.C: "Take up a contact sport such as soccer or basketball to strengthen your body."
RN-S18-14.D: "Floss vigorously twice a day to keep your gums healthy."

RN-S18-15.A: Hypotension from anemia and blood loss

RN-S18-17.A: "Perform the exam just once a year, such as on your birthday, so that it's easy for you to remember to do it."
RN-S18-17.C: "You only need to examine your testicles if you notice pain or discomfort in the scrotum."
RN-S18-17.D: "Squeeze each testicle firmly between your thumb and fingers to check for areas of pain."

RN-S18-18.A: "You can safely resume sexual activity tonight, since the single dose of azithromycin starts working right away."
RN-S18-18.C: "Your sexual partners don't need to be tested or treated, because the single dose of medication you took will clear the infection."
RN-S18-18.D: "After this treatment, you'll be immune to chlamydia, so you won't be able to catch it again in the future."

RN-S18-19.A: Pinpoint pupils, bradycardia, hypothermia, and marked drowsiness with slurred speech
RN-S18-19.C: Slow, shallow respirations, sedation, and slurred speech
RN-S18-19.D: Hypotension, constricted pupils, and a slow heart rate of 48/min

RN-S19-01.B: A client 4 hours after shock wave lithotripsy who has pink-tinged urine and mild bruising over the left flank
RN-S19-01.C: A client with polycystic kidney disease requesting a refill of a BP medication before discharge
RN-S19-01.D: A client with benign prostatic hyperplasia who reports nocturia two to three times each night

RN-S19-02.A: The client ate a light breakfast of dry toast and apple juice about 2 hours before the scheduled cardioversion procedure
RN-S19-02.C: The client took the usual morning dose of digoxin with a small sip of water before arriving
RN-S19-02.D: The client's potassium level is 3.1 mEq/L on the basic metabolic panel drawn early this morning

RN-S19-03.B: "You can ignore any shocks unless you have more than five of them in a single day, since a shock just means the device is doing its job to protect you."
RN-S19-03.C: "You will need to avoid all types of physical activity for the rest of your life so the device doesn't fire by mistake."
RN-S19-03.D: "Family members and friends will be seriously injured if they happen to be touching you when the device delivers a shock."

RN-S19-05.B: Oral ibuprofen 400 mg with food and water
RN-S19-05.C: A warm, moist compress applied over the painful eye
RN-S19-05.D: IV fluids only, with no other treatment

RN-S19-07.A: "Take a double dose on the morning of your surgery so that your blood sugar stays under control during the hours you're not able to eat."
RN-S19-07.C: "This medication lowers your blood sugar by causing your pancreas to release more insulin after each meal you eat."
RN-S19-07.D: "An added benefit of this medication is that it helps prevent urinary tract infections for as long as you take it."

RN-S19-08.A: Pumps deliver only long-acting insulin, so the client's glucose is likely to drop too low during the night
RN-S19-08.C: Disconnection for a few hours has no effect on the client's glucose or ketone levels
RN-S19-08.D: The client will develop hypoglycemia from the extra insulin given when the tubing reconnects

RN-S19-09.A: "Unfortunately, there is still no effective treatment for chronic hepatitis C."
RN-S19-09.C: "A vaccine given in a series of three shots will cure the infection."
RN-S19-09.D: "Treatment is only recommended for people who already have liver failure."

RN-S19-10.A: Frequent watery stools every 15 to 30 minutes since starting the prep
RN-S19-10.C: Clear, yellow liquid stools with no solid material
RN-S19-10.D: Mild abdominal fullness and bloating after drinking the prep

RN-S19-11.A: Absent bowel sounds with a rigid, board-like abdomen and marked rebound tenderness
RN-S19-11.C: Frequent bloody diarrhea with crampy lower abdominal pain and urgency
RN-S19-11.D: Left lower quadrant pain that is relieved by having a bowel movement

RN-S19-12.A: Dairy products such as milk, cheese, yogurt, and ice cream at any meal
RN-S19-12.C: All fruits, including citrus fruits, berries, and melons
RN-S19-12.D: Acetaminophen at any dose, even for a mild headache

RN-S19-14.A: "You'll be able to speak normally again in a few days, once the swelling goes down."
RN-S19-14.C: "Keep the stoma tightly covered with plastic wrap at all times to keep it clean."
RN-S19-14.D: "You can still breathe through your nose and mouth if the stoma gets blocked."

RN-S19-15.A: Elevated platelets and low liver enzymes with no hemolysis
RN-S19-15.C: Low hemoglobin with normal liver enzymes and platelets
RN-S19-15.D: Elevated serum glucose with ketones in the urine

RN-S19-16.A: Apply firm, steady fundal pressure at the top of the uterus with both hands to help push the baby's impacted shoulders out as quickly as possible
RN-S19-16.C: Use a gloved hand to push the fetal head back up into the vagina while the client stops pushing for now
RN-S19-16.D: Place the client in Trendelenburg position, with the head of the bed lowered below the level of the hips

RN-S19-17.A: "I can start trying to get pregnant again right away, since the mole has been completely removed."
RN-S19-17.C: "I don't need any follow-up visits or blood tests now that the procedure is finished."
RN-S19-17.D: "A rising hCG level over the next few weeks is a good sign that I'm healing."

RN-S19-18.A: Immediately after the client's last use of opioids, before any of the withdrawal symptoms have had a chance to begin
RN-S19-18.C: Only after the client has completed at least 2 weeks of complete abstinence from all opioids and alcohol
RN-S19-18.D: At the same time as a dose of a full-agonist opioid such as oxycodone, to ease the transition

PN-S18-01.A: Have the client stand 5 feet from the wall chart and read the smallest line that is possible with both eyes open
PN-S18-01.C: Test both eyes together only, with the client wearing their reading glasses for the test
PN-S18-01.D: Have the client read the letters from a small handheld card held at about arm's length

PN-S18-02.A: Cover the affected eye with a sterile eye patch and arrange to transport the worker to the hospital emergency department right away
PN-S18-02.C: Have the worker rub the eye gently with a clean tissue to remove the chemical and relieve the burning
PN-S18-02.D: Apply an antibiotic eye ointment and have the worker rest quietly with the eye closed until the burning stops

PN-S18-03.A: "You can wear it in the shower so that you're still able to hear people while you're washing."
PN-S18-03.C: "Wipe it down with rubbing alcohol every day to kill any germs that collect on it."
PN-S18-03.D: "Store it in the bathroom cabinet so that it's close by when you get ready each morning."

PN-S18-04.A: Stand right next to the client and shout directly into the better ear so that every word can be heard very clearly
PN-S18-04.C: Continue speaking to the client while walking away or turning to do other tasks around the room
PN-S18-04.D: Exaggerate your lip movements dramatically and speak very slowly, pausing after every single word

PN-S18-05.A: Keep the room lights dim at all times to reduce glare and help protect what remains of the client's central field of vision
PN-S18-05.C: Rearrange the furniture in the room often so the client can practice finding the way around safely
PN-S18-05.D: Encourage the client to continue driving, but only at night, when there is less traffic on the roads

PN-S18-07.A: The client's favorite music to play during the procedure
PN-S18-07.C: Whether the client wears glasses or contacts
PN-S18-07.D: The client's blood type and Rh factor

PN-S18-08.A: "Try to stand for long periods throughout the day, since standing in one place will strengthen your leg muscles."
PN-S18-08.C: "Cross your legs at the knees whenever you sit down, to help support the veins in your legs."
PN-S18-08.D: "Wear tight knee-high socks with snug elastic tops every day to give your legs more support."

PN-S18-09.A: "Strain during bowel movements so that you empty your bowels completely."
PN-S18-09.C: "Sit on the toilet for long periods until you feel completely empty."
PN-S18-09.D: "Avoid drinking fluids so that your stools are not as loose."

PN-S18-11.A: "Keep your wrist bent in a flexed position while you type at the keyboard, which helps to rest the tendons."
PN-S18-11.C: "Sleep with both wrists bent and tucked under your pillow to keep them warm and comfortable."
PN-S18-11.D: "Squeeze a soft stress ball for several hours each day to strengthen your hand and grip."

PN-S18-12.A: Complete bed rest for several weeks, until the pain and fatigue have gone away completely
PN-S18-12.C: High-impact exercise, such as running or jumping rope, every day for at least an hour
PN-S18-12.D: Avoiding all physical activity permanently once the client has had a flare

PN-S18-13.A: "Drink a cup of hot coffee or tea as soon as you feel a hot flash starting to come on."
PN-S18-13.C: "Take extra blankets to bed so that you stay warm and cozy through the night."
PN-S18-13.D: "Avoid all types of exercise and stay as still as possible during the day."

PN-S18-14.A: "The HPV vaccine is only given after a child becomes sexually active, not before."
PN-S18-14.C: "The HPV vaccine is only recommended for girls and young women, not for boys."
PN-S18-14.D: "The first dose of the vaccine is recommended at age 30, during routine screening."

PN-S18-15.A: "Once I finish the antiviral medication, the virus will be cured completely, so I won't have to worry about having any more outbreaks."
PN-S18-15.C: "I can't spread herpes to anyone as long as I don't have any sores, so condoms are only needed during outbreaks."
PN-S18-15.D: "I only need to be treated once, and after that the infection won't come back or be spread to my partner."

PN-S18-16.A: "Every man needs to have a PSA blood test once a month, starting at age 40, so that prostate cancer can be caught as early as possible."
PN-S18-16.C: "PSA tests are never recommended for any men at any age, because the results are just not useful."
PN-S18-16.D: "Only men who are over age 80 need to have a PSA test, so you can wait until then to think about it."

PN-S18-17.A: Place the infant prone to sleep at night, with the head turned to one side on a firm, flat crib mattress
PN-S18-17.C: Allow the infant to suck on a pacifier as often as needed to soothe crying after surgery
PN-S18-17.D: Clean the suture line roughly with a dry cotton ball to remove all of the crusts

PN-S18-18.A: "Remove the harness each night at bedtime so that your baby can sleep more comfortably until the morning feeding."
PN-S18-18.C: "Apply a layer of lotion and baby powder under the straps each day to protect your baby's delicate skin."
PN-S18-18.D: "Tighten the straps yourself whenever your baby kicks a lot or the harness starts to seem loose."

PN-S18-19.A: Place the newborn supine on a soft blanket with a small rolled towel under the hips for support
PN-S18-19.C: Leave the sac uncovered and open to the air so that it can dry out and form a protective crust
PN-S18-19.D: Use standard latex gloves for all care and procedures, since the newborn has not yet shown any sign of a latex allergy

PN-S18-20.A: Give an antiemetic and let the child sleep it off
PN-S18-20.C: Encourage the child to drink more fluids to prevent dehydration
PN-S18-20.D: Document the findings and review them at the next visit

PN-S18-21.A: "Give your child children's aspirin every 4 to 6 hours as needed to bring down the fever and ease discomfort."
PN-S18-21.C: "Your child can go back to school tomorrow, even if some new spots are still appearing on the skin."
PN-S18-21.D: "Letting your child scratch the itchy spots will actually help the lesions crust over and heal faster."

PN-S18-22.A: "Stop the antibiotic as soon as your child's sore throat improves."
PN-S18-22.C: "Use throat lozenges and warm tea instead of the antibiotics."
PN-S18-22.D: "Save any leftover antibiotics for the next time your child gets sick."

PN-S18-23.A: The test shows that the fetus is in distress and may need to be delivered right away
PN-S18-23.C: The test results are unclear, so the test must be repeated immediately before the client leaves
PN-S18-23.D: The client has started early labor and should be admitted to the labor and delivery unit

PN-S19-01.A: Apply ice to the area and have him rest for a few hours in the clinic
PN-S19-01.C: Give ibuprofen for the pain and send him back to class to see if it improves
PN-S19-01.D: Tell him it's most likely just a pulled groin muscle from gym class

PN-S19-02.A: Give the client a personal phone number so they can stay in touch after discharge
PN-S19-02.C: Start exploring new problems in depth during the last few sessions
PN-S19-02.D: End the relationship without warning at the last scheduled session

PN-S19-03.A: "Take it only when you feel a panic attack starting, and it will work right away."
PN-S19-03.C: "It works within minutes to calm you down, just like lorazepam does."
PN-S19-03.D: "It is highly addictive, so you should take it only for a few days."

PN-S19-04.A: Tell the client firmly that the symptoms are imaginary, since all of the medical tests have come back normal
PN-S19-04.C: Ignore any new physical complaints the client reports, since all of the previous medical workups have come back negative
PN-S19-04.D: Encourage the client to keep asking the provider for more diagnostic tests until a physical cause is found

PN-S19-05.A: "Children with Down syndrome can't safely take part in any sports, so gymnastics is out of the question."
PN-S19-05.C: "There are no special considerations, so your child can start gymnastics classes right away like any other child."
PN-S19-05.D: "Swimming is the only sport that children with Down syndrome are allowed to take part in safely."

PN-S19-06.A: Feed the child while lying flat on the back to help keep the head and neck still
PN-S19-06.C: Feed the child as quickly as possible so the child does not become tired during the meal
PN-S19-06.D: Offer large bites of food on the spoon to reduce the total time needed for each meal

PN-S19-08.C: A positive Babinski reflex in both feet

PN-S19-09.A: Perform abdominal thrusts with the infant held upright against your body, repeating them until the food comes out or the infant stops responding
PN-S19-09.C: Perform a blind finger sweep of the back of the infant's mouth to try to find and remove the piece of food
PN-S19-09.D: Hold the infant upside down by the ankles and shake gently, repeating until the piece of food comes out

PN-S19-10.A: "Yes, that's fine. Children's vitamins are harmless, even if your child eats a few extra of them by mistake one day."
PN-S19-10.C: "Only adult vitamins are dangerous to children, so the children's chewable vitamins can stay on the counter."
PN-S19-10.D: "Keep them in the door of the refrigerator so they stay fresh and are easy for the family to find."

PN-S19-11.B: "This rash is a sign of a serious infection that needs antibiotics."
PN-S19-11.C: "This is an allergic reaction to the formula, so you'll need to switch brands."
PN-S19-11.D: "This rash means the baby is too hot and needs fewer blankets."

PN-S19-12.A: "The newborn hearing test is usually only done when there's a known family history of hearing loss."
PN-S19-12.C: "The test checks for any ear infections that newborns can sometimes develop after birth."
PN-S19-12.D: "Hearing tests aren't really necessary until the child is ready to start school."

PN-S19-13.A: "You can feed your child a regular diet as the child grows, once the newborn period is over."
PN-S19-13.C: "PKU usually goes away on its own by about age 2, so the special diet will only be needed for a short time."
PN-S19-13.D: "Give your child extra protein, such as meat, eggs, and milk, every day to support healthy growth."

PN-S19-14.A: "The circumcision should be done right away, before your baby is discharged home from the hospital."
PN-S19-14.C: "Hypospadias usually requires no treatment, because it tends to correct itself as the baby grows."
PN-S19-14.D: "Doing a routine circumcision will fix the hypospadias at the same time, so no other surgery is needed."

PN-S19-16.A: "Thaw frozen milk quickly in the microwave for about 30 seconds on high, then swirl it well and test a few drops on the inside of your wrist before you feed the baby."
PN-S19-16.C: "If you thaw more milk than your baby drinks, you can safely put the extra back in the freezer and refreeze it to use for a later feeding."
PN-S19-16.D: "Freshly pumped milk can be left out on the kitchen counter overnight at room temperature and then used for the first feeding in the morning."

PN-S19-17.A: "Take an iron supplement every day with a glass of orange juice to keep your energy up."
PN-S19-17.C: "Eat raw oysters and clams regularly so you get extra zinc in your diet."
PN-S19-17.D: "Cook in cast-iron pans as often as possible to add iron to your food."

PN-S19-18.A: Clamp the nephrostomy tube whenever the client gets up to walk so the bag does not pull on the site
PN-S19-18.C: Irrigate the tube routinely every shift with large volumes of sterile saline to keep it from clogging
PN-S19-18.D: Place the drainage bag on top of the client's abdomen while the client is resting in bed so it stays in view

PN-S19-19.A: "Limit how much you drink for the next few days to reduce your urine output and your discomfort."
PN-S19-19.C: "Call your provider immediately if you notice any pink-tinged urine, since it means you are bleeding."
PN-S19-19.D: "You can stop straining your urine after the first day, since the stone has already been broken up into pieces."

PN-S19-20.A: "Rinse with an alcohol-based mouthwash several times a day to keep your mouth feeling fresh and clean."
PN-S19-20.C: "Eat dry, crunchy foods such as crackers, toast, and chips to help stimulate your saliva."
PN-S19-20.D: "Sip on sugary sodas or sweet tea throughout the day to keep your mouth feeling moist."

PN-S19-21.A: "Sit with a fan blowing directly on your face to cool your eyes."
PN-S19-21.C: "Rub your eyes gently several times a day to stimulate tears."
PN-S19-21.D: "Wear your contact lenses all day to protect the surface of your eyes."

PN-S19-22.A: Performing advanced procedures that are outside the nurse's training to try to save the victim's life
PN-S19-22.C: Sending the victim a bill afterward for the emergency nursing care that was provided at the scene
PN-S19-22.D: Leaving the victim once care has started, without handing off care to another rescuer or EMS

PN-S19-23.A: Require every client to sign a do-not-resuscitate order as part of the standard admission paperwork packet
PN-S19-23.C: Choose a health care proxy for the client from the staff if the client has not already named one
PN-S19-23.D: Keep any advance directives out of the medical record to protect the client's privacy and wishes
